kept.spine: The arrangements at Spitzplatz cover what the town has to cover, and nothing spare. A second call on them at the same time would set the town to choosing which pressure it leaves alone.

kept.poolKey: Invasion & War: walls with NO force
kept.spine: The town walls are kept up. No soldiers of the town's own stand behind them.
faces: {elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary before anything else, and where the line runs is the older argument.
A night patrolman says the walk along the top of the walls is nobody's to pay for, and that he walks it anyway.
A woman who brought a matter to the court says what is argued there about the walls is always who owes the work on them, and never who would hold them.
The townsfolk have seen the walls kept and nobody on them, and take it that nobody is coming.

kept.poolKey: Internal Security: full legal chain (court AND prison)
kept.spine: A complaint brought here is heard at the courthouse, and the town has cells to hold the man it names until then.
faces: A clerk in the hall says nobody waits at the courthouse longer than the matter in front of theirs takes.
A rider who stopped a night says he was told where the court sits and never told when.
A bailiff says a stranger's complaint is heard like any other, and that whether the stranger stays for the hearing is the stranger's own affair.
A woman at the long table says a man is called in for who he knows and let out for what he can pay.
One of the watch says the wage is the same whether the night is quiet or a man is walked to the cells.
A soldier reckons a stranger stopped at the gate is the garrison's until his business is asked. After that he is the watch's.
The dyers' warden says the trades pay twice for a man held at the court, in the man and in the work standing idle behind him.
The stallholders say a stranger cheated at the market is told where to bring the matter, and that a stallholder cheated by a stranger is told the same after the stranger has gone.
The men who hold the way in say a stranger with a complaint against him waits at the gate until somebody comes down from the courthouse for him.

kept.spine: The grain store and the merchant warehouses are the town's own, and the feeding and supplying of the town would hold through a hard season.
faces: A man who walks the circuit says the purse he is paid from is the last one the hall opens.
The soldiers say they are paid out of the same purse and in the same order.
One of the aldermen says the store is full and the wage can wait on the season.
A master of one of the crafts reckons the trades put the provision in the store and the hall put the shortfall in the wage.
A drover says the store door smells of grain and the talk at the tavern is all of the wage.
A local priest holds that the parish asks the town for nothing beyond what the town has already promised it.
The mayor says the town is provided for, and asked about the wage, says the town is provided for.
A clerk of the court says the watch's wage is not a matter anybody brings to the court.

kept.poolKey: Disasters & Famine: granary AND parish care only
kept.spine: The town keeps a grain store and its parish churches, and no sick house. Whoever tends a sick man here comes out of a parish.
faces: A warden of one of the parishes says a stranger asks the town for a sick house and is given a person instead.
A woman who sells at the market says grain is easy to buy here and hard to keep for anybody without a door of their own.
A carter at the tavern says strangers walk up the road to look at the grain store and nobody born here does.
The guard captain says strangers ask where the grain is kept and that nobody has ever asked where the sick are kept.
A journeyman says what a stranger takes for provision is a store the trades filled and cannot open.
One who waits on the court says a stranger's questions about the grain store are the ordinary ones and the questions about the sick are new.

kept.spine: The safety of Spitzplatz sits where either side could take it. A thinner watch would move it, and so would a bolder hand on the other side.

kept.poolKey: First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)
kept.spine: What the town says of its own safety is what a place says to a newcomer. A longer acquaintance would be given a different account.
The streets of Spitzplatz are quiet, and the quiet is kept by the people who lose money whenever the watch is called to them.
Every way into the town runs through a gate the town keeps. Whatever comes at the place comes at an opening of the town's own choosing.
The town watch walks the streets after dark. What the people here count as keeping them safe is the walking and not the walls.
The charter hall keeps a board of work, and the work on it is the sort that walls and a night walk are no answer to. A stranger who comes looking finds the board full.
The alchemist's shop is counted among the town's provision against the sort of trouble a wall and a night walk never see coming.
The town walls around Spitzplatz are sound, and the keeping of them takes very nearly all the town lays out for its defence.
